text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait to host a trade fair for products made in the United States.

- Central Bank Governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al-Sabah says Kuwait Stock Exchange developments reassuring. Some parliamentarians have voiced fears that the bourse, which set new records last week, could be heading towards a crash.

- Gulf oil sales drop after Iraq's deal with the United Nations, industry experts say. The December deal allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over a renewable six-month period. Iraq has been under strict U.N. sanctions since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
- Kuwait share index rises 49 points to 2309.1.
- Ban on use of mobile telephones while driving sought.
- Police arrest 25 women, 15 men in attempt to eliminate prostitution in the conservative Gulf Arab state.

- Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali expresses hope that relations with Kuwait would improve. Ties between the two Arab states were strained due to Amman's perceived sympathy with Baghdad during its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.
